inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average diluted shares Q2 2026 (quarter ended 2026-06-26, 10-Q XBRL WeightedAverageNumberOfDilutedSharesOutstanding). Held FLAT: SBC plus equity-award withholding tax is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting as well would double-charge. Masimo was an all-cash deal, so there is no non-SBC issuance to model.
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL ShareBasedCompensation (cash-flow add-back), TTM to Jun-2026 = FY2025 298 + H1-26 151 - H1-25 152 = 297; plus FY2025 PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation 69 (no combined figure published) = 366
inputs.fy0: TTM Jun-2026, pro forma full-year Masimo
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free 4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.9 -> cost of equity ~8.8%; pre-tax cost of debt ~4.6% (-> ~3.6% after tax) at ~12% debt weight on market values (net debt 22.2bn vs market cap ~159bn) -> WACC ~8.2%. One WACC across all scenarios: risk is carried in the scenario paths and weights, not a premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases (~$1.3bn liability): lease cost is already inside operating expense and therefore inside EBITDA; lease liabilities are NOT added to net debt. lease_cost_pct_path = 0 to avoid a second charge.
inputs.notes:
MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build (dcf-methods routing row 'operating company'). Danaher is a life-sciences tools / bioprocessing / diagnostics operating company with a recurring consumables base; none of the bank/REIT/holdco rows apply. First valuation of DHR (no MEMORY entry). US filer: owner-fcf-adaptations not required (USD flows and quote, US GAAP operating leases inside EBITDA, SBC-positive market).

FY0 AND MASIMO: Masimo closed 2026-06-10 for $9.84bn cash (XBRL PaymentsToAcquireBusinessesNetOfCashAcquired H1-26). The net debt anchor is the 2026-06-26 balance sheet, which already carries the acquisition debt; so the revenue base must carry Masimo too, or the model would pay for Masimo without owning its flows. base_revenue = TTM Jun-26 revenue 25,107 (FY25 24,568 + H1-26 12,216 - H1-25 11,677) - ~95 of Masimo stub already booked + ~2,200 annualised Masimo continuing (healthcare, post consumer-audio sale) revenue = ~27,200. The Masimo run-rate is an estimate; replace with disclosed figures from the Q3-26 10-Q. Year 1 of the projection is Jul-26 to Jun-27.

NET DEBT: LongTermDebt (total incl. current portion) 26,558 at 2026-06-26 (noncurrent 25,147 + current 1,411) less cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash 4,348 = 22,210. DATA ISSUE: Metrics.csv TotalDebt for Q1 2026 (19,407) and Q2 2026 (27,969) equals LongTermDebt PLUS DebtCurrent, i.e. double-counts the current portion (27,969 = 26,558 + 1,411); FY2025 18,420 is correct. Should be fixed via make fix. Metrics.csv also has no CashAndEquivalents after FY2019 (XBRL tag changed to CashCashEquivalentsRestrictedCash...).

OWNER FCF: reported FCF TTM 5,466 (OCF - capex) - SBC incl. equity-award taxes 366 = 5,100. Interest income NOT stripped: DHR is net-debt (the H1-26 interest income of 88 was earned on cash pre-funded for Masimo and is gone). Reported FCF is after cash interest paid; the DCF is unlevered and deducts net debt instead, so the valuation flows are built from EBITDA, not from last_fcf.

COMPONENTS: EBITDA margin is pre-SBC GAAP EBITDA: FY25 op income 4,690 + depreciation 750 + amortisation 1,697 + SBC 298 = 7,435 (30.3%, depressed by impairment/restructuring); H1-26 2,471 + 389 + 897 + 151 = 3,908 (32.0%). Masimo dilutes ~0.5pp at close (Diagnostics margin -160bp in Q2). D&A path is DEPRECIATION ONLY (~3.1-3.2% of revenue); acquired-intangible amortisation is non-cash and excluded from both the tax base and the add-back, and the cash tax rate is calibrated to EBITA accordingly: cash taxes paid FY25 1,200 / EBITA (4,690 + 1,697) 6,387 = 18.8%; FY24 1,300 / ~6,400 = ~20%. Capex FY23-25 5.8%/5.8%/4.7%, H1-26 4.1%. Working capital negative capture (manufacturer/distributor: receivables + inventory exceed payables) at -15% of the revenue increase.

BUYBACKS: DHR is an active repurchaser (FY24 5,979; FY25 3,088; H1-26 894) - the flat count is funded, not just a modelling convention. Dividends ~0.9bn/yr are a use of owner FCF, not a deduction.

NOT MODELLED: StatLab (announced, expected to close by YE26; price undisclosed in the inputs available) - neither its cost nor its flows are in the model. Pension deficit and legal reserves not bridged (immaterial vs a ~$180bn EV).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: equity_5yr_cagr 5.7% tempered toward mid-single-digit industry growth; all trailing CAGRs span the COVID boom (FY21-22) and bust plus the Sep-2023 Veralto spin, so none is a clean run-rate
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5y CAGR 5.7% vs revenue 5y 2.0% and EPS 5y 0.4% (and 3y revenue -2.7%, EPS -19.7%): divergence >30%. Causes: COVID testing/bioprocess peak in FY21-22 then destocking, Veralto spin-off (Sep-2023) removing ~$5bn of revenue, Abcam acquisition (Dec-2023). Equity growth reflects retained earnings and FX, not organic growth.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes; no interest-income strip as DHR is net-debt): FY2020 5,172, FY2022 7,007, FY2025 4,893. SBC-adjusted and reported FCF CAGRs are close (SBC ~1.2% of revenue), so SBC is not driving the gap; the decline is the post-COVID normalisation plus the Veralto spin.

base.narrative: Core growth 3-4% in FY26 (guidance) with ~$100m bioprocess revenue slipping into 2027 and the respiratory-testing roll-off peaking in H2-26, then mid-single-digit core growth as bioprocessing recovers to high-single-digit and Life Sciences holds. Masimo margins pulled up by DBS over 3-4 years to a ~32.5% pre-SBC EBITDA margin, in line with H1-26 ex-Masimo.

bull.narrative: Bioprocessing re-accelerates to double-digit as biologics/cell-and-gene capacity utilisation normalises and the 2027 push-outs land; Cytiva's chromatography-resin lock-in holds pricing; Masimo cross-sells into Beckman/Cepheid hospital accounts and DBS lifts its margin to group level; operating leverage takes pre-SBC EBITDA to ~34.5%, near the non-COVID peak.

bear.narrative: The 2026 bioprocess push-out is the start of a second destocking leg rather than timing; China VBP keeps compressing diagnostics pricing; respiratory testing keeps rolling off; Masimo integration stalls under a new CEO and its lower margin permanently dilutes Diagnostics. Growth stays at low-single-digit and margins stick at ~30%, with a lower exit multiple for a slower tools business.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-single-digit core growth after a soft FY26 (3-4% core guide, respiratory headwind ~250bp in Q3-26, ~$100m bioprocess revenue into 2027), full-year Masimo from the close, and DBS lifting Masimo's lower margin so group pre-SBC EBITDA reaches ~32.5% by year 4.
scenario_narratives.bull: Bioprocessing recovery runs to double-digit, Cytiva resin share (~80%) and validated-workflow lock-in hold price, Masimo becomes a genuine second Diagnostics growth platform, and margins expand toward ~34.5% - a return to the DBS compounding record.
scenario_narratives.bear: A second bioprocess destocking leg, China VBP pricing, the respiratory roll-off and a stalled Masimo integration during the CEO handover keep growth at 2.5-3.5% and margins flat at ~30%; the market stops paying a compounder multiple (16x exit cap).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 20%: bioprocess demand has already shown one violent destocking cycle and the 2026 push-out revives it, while Masimo integration and a CEO change (1 Oct 2026) coincide. Base 50%: guidance and the consumables base support it. Bull trimmed to 30%: it needs bioprocess recovery, Masimo margin uplift and China stabilisation to all go right; the balance sheet (ND/EBITDA ~2.6x) is no solvency risk, so bear is not higher.

valuation_philosophy.summary: House basis values Danaher on unlevered owner FCF with SBC and equity-award withholding fully expensed, share count held flat, and the post-Masimo balance sheet deducted. The revenue base is pro forma for a full year of Masimo so the acquisition debt and the acquired flows are matched. Acquired-intangible amortisation is kept out of both the tax base and the cash flows; the cash tax rate is calibrated to EBITA from actual cash taxes paid.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value is roughly two-thirds of EV; the 20x cap binds near Gordon at 8.2%/3.0%, so exit-multiple assumptions dominate
Masimo annualised revenue (~$2.2bn) and margin are estimates until the Q3-26 10-Q discloses the post-close contribution
Bioprocess destocking recurrence (the axis between base and bear)
StatLab acquisition not modelled (cost and flows both excluded)
Metrics.csv TotalDebt for Q1/Q2 2026 double-counts current debt; the DCF uses the XBRL LongTermDebt total instead
